caveats: OCR not bundled by default: confirmed. `npm run build` does NOT need any OCR download or API (vendor:ocr is a separate opt-in script that downloads eng.traineddata from raw.githubusercontent.com). But the resulting build cannot do Deep OCR (README documents this) AND cannot unlock password-protected PDFs on the web: src/utils/qpdfUnlock.ts loads ${BASE_URL}qpdf/{qpdf.js,qpdf.wasm,worker.js}, which only .github/workflows/deploy.yml copies from node_modules/qpdf-run before building (README's 'serve dist with any static host' note omits this). decryptInput() is used by Unlock and by Merge/Split/Signature/Watermark/Metadata and other engines for locked inputs, so those fail with 'could not be unlocked' on locked PDFs. Runtime third-party requests: none by default (tesseract jsdelivr default is overridden by explicit local paths). localStorage for theme/settings. og:url/twitter meta hardcode potatameister.github.io. why: Would be a strong fit (1.5k-star, privacy-first, client-only PDF tool with hash routing), but see reason.
reason: Anybuild/upstream build mismatch that misleads users: Anybuild runs only `npm run build`, while the maintainer's web deploy also vendors the OCR engine and the qpdf WASM unlock engine into public/. A badge deploy would ship a PaperKnife whose password unlock (and every tool on locked PDFs) and Deep OCR fail, with a README promising 'Password protect and unlock PDFs'. Fixing it needs a build-script change (e.g. folding the qpdf copy into `build`), which is out of README-only scope. Re-qualify if upstream moves the qpdf copy into the build script or the coordinator accepts a README note documenting the missing unlock/OCR. PR #17 is NOT the reason (author-closed, no maintainer objection).
